For new tables, use Inferlo [models](database.md): validated inserts and updates, typed queries, relations, pagination and generated migrations (`inferlo db migrate`). Inferlo models expect a `uuid` `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` columns and snake_case column names, so existing tables that differ are best left with your current code.

## 7. Move the tests

```ts
// Before: a testing module and supertest
const moduleRef = await Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [AppModule] }).compile();
const nest = moduleRef.createNestApplication();
await nest.init();
await request(nest.getHttpServer()).post("/tickets").set("authorization", `Bearer ${token}`).send({ title: "Printer" }).expect(201);

// After: in-process, no server, port or module compilation, signed in as a test user
import { readJson } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/testing";

const res = await app.request("/tickets", { method: "POST", json: { title: "Printer" }, as: { id: "u1", roles: [] } });
const ticket = await readJson(res, 201);
```

End-to-end tests through the Nest app (`supertest`) keep working during the migration, because the Inferlo app is mounted in it.

## 8. Remove NestJS

When the last controller is gone, start the Inferlo app directly and remove Nest:

```ts
// src/server.ts
import { app } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const server = await app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log(`Listening on http://localhost:${server.port}`);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => void app.close({ delayMs: 5000 }));
```

Then remove `@nestjs/*`, `reflect-metadata`, `class-validator`, `class-transformer` and `rxjs` if nothing else uses them, and turn off `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` in `tsconfig.json`. Compare your app with a new project from `npx @browserlessapi/inferlo new` for the recommended layout, configuration and AGENTS.md for AI coding tools.

## Checklist

- [ ] Inferlo app mounted with `nest.use(toNodeHandler(app, { fallthrough: true }))` before `listen()`
- [ ] One auth check shared by Nest guards and Inferlo
- [ ] Each moved route: schemas for its input, the right `auth`, `status(201)` where clients expect it, the Nest method removed, a test with `app.request`
- [ ] Nest feature modules turned into Inferlo modules, services into plain functions in `provides`
- [ ] Clients told about the new error format, if they read error bodies
- [ ] NestJS removed, `app.listen()` and `app.close()` in `src/server.ts`

If you only want Inferlo's AI features inside NestJS and no migration, use `InferloModule` from [`@browserlessapi/inferlo/nestjs`](integrations.md#nestjs-1) instead.

---

# Migrate from Hono

This guide moves an existing Hono app to Inferlo one route at a time. The app keeps running, on the same runtime (Node.js, Bun, Deno or Cloudflare Workers), and keeps its URLs during the whole migration: Hono answers the routes you have not moved yet, Inferlo answers the rest. Nothing has to be rewritten in one go.

Both are built on Web standards (`Request`, `Response`, `fetch`), and Inferlo's routes look like Hono's on purpose, so most handlers move with small changes. What you gain on every route you move: validation and types from one schema without a separate validator middleware, routes private by default, the same error format everywhere (`ILxxxx` codes), a database layer with migrations, rate limits, background jobs, an OpenAPI document and an MCP server generated from the routes, and AI models through `ctx.ai`. See [comparison](comparison.md) for the bigger picture.

## 1. Add Inferlo next to Hono

```bash
npm install @browserlessapi/inferlo
```

Create an empty Inferlo app beside your Hono code, for example in `src/inferlo/app.ts`:

```ts
// src/inferlo/app.ts
import { createApp } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { auth } from "./auth.ts";
import * as tickets from "./routes/tickets.ts";

export const app = createApp({
  name: "helpdesk",
  routes: [tickets],
  auth,
  logging: { requests: true },
});
```

Pass every request Hono does not answer to Inferlo, with a catch-all **after** all your Hono routes:

```ts
// src/index.ts (your existing Hono entry point)
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { app as inferlo } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const hono = new Hono();

hono.get("/users/:id", getUser);     // not moved yet: Hono answers
hono.route("/books", books);         // sub-apps too

hono.all("*", (c) => inferlo.fetch(c.req.raw)); // last: everything else goes to Inferlo, including 404s

export default hono;
```

Hono matches routes in the order they were added, so its own routes win and every other request, including other methods on the same path, reaches Inferlo with the original `Request`. Inferlo routes it, or answers `404` with IL2001. Inferlo reads the body itself; keep Hono middleware that reads bodies (validators) on Hono routes only, not on `*`.

Middleware added with `hono.use(...)` before the catch-all also runs for Inferlo's requests. That is fine for logging; for CORS, security headers and request ids, Inferlo has its own (step 3), so scope Hono's to the Hono routes or remove it once Inferlo answers most routes.

If you would rather keep the new routes under their own path for a while, mount the app there instead: `hono.mount("/v2", inferlo.fetch)` (Hono removes `/v2` before Inferlo sees the path). To use only Inferlo's AI features in Hono handlers, see [`inferloAI()`](integrations.md#hono).

## 2. Move one route

Before, in Hono with Zod and `@hono/zod-validator`:

```ts
hono.post(
  "/tickets",
  requireUser,
  zValidator("json", z.object({
    title: z.string().min(3).max(200),
    priority: z.enum(["low", "normal", "urgent"]).default("normal"),
  })),
  async (c) => {
    const body = c.req.valid("json");
    const ticket = await tickets.insert({ ...body, ownerId: c.get("user").id });
    return c.json(ticket, 201);
  },
);
```

After, in Inferlo:

```ts
// src/inferlo/routes/tickets.ts
import { route, t } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { tickets } from "../../db.ts"; // your existing data access code

export const createTicket = route
  .post("/tickets", {
    body: t.object({
      title: t.string().min(3).max(200),
      priority: t.enum(["low", "normal", "urgent"]).default("normal"),
    }),
    summary: "Create a ticket",
  })
  .handle(async ({ body, user, status }) => {
    status(201);
    return tickets.insert({ ...body, ownerId: user.id });
  });
```

Then delete the Hono route. Requests to `POST /tickets` now reach Inferlo, at the same URL.

- `t.*` schemas read like Zod: `z.string().min(3)` is `t.string().min(3)`, `z.enum([...])` is `t.enum([...])`, `.optional()` and `.default()` are the same. The schema replaces the validator middleware: invalid input gets `422` with IL1001 and every problem listed, and `body` is typed. `query` and `params` schemas replace the `"query"` and `"param"` validators.
- The route is private by default: `user` is the signed-in user, and requests without one get `401` (IL3001). This replaces `requireUser`, `bearerAuth` or `jwt` middleware. Add `auth: "public"` to routes anyone may call, or a role name such as `auth: "admin"`.
- Return the value instead of `c.json(value)`; call `status(201)` instead of `c.json(value, 201)`. `undefined` sends `204`. A `Response` is sent as it is, so `return c.body(...)` style code becomes `return new Response(...)`.
- Throw `notFound()`, `forbidden()` or `httpError(409, "...")` instead of `HTTPException`.
- The error format changes to Inferlo's `{ "error": { "code", "message", ... } }`. If clients parse error bodies, tell them, or move routes in groups that one client uses.

## 3. Map Hono concepts to Inferlo

| Hono | Inferlo |
|---|---|
| `hono.get(path, handler)` | `export const x = route.get(path, options).handle(handler)` in a routes file, registered with `createApp({ routes: [file] })` |
| `c.req.param()`, `c.req.query()`, `await c.req.json()` | `params`, `query`, `body` in the handler context, validated by schemas ([schemas](schema.md)) |
| `zValidator`, `validator()` | `body`, `query` and `params` options with `t.*` schemas |
| `c.json(value, status)`, `c.text()`, `c.body()` | `return value` and `status(code)`; return a `Response` for anything else |
| `c.header(name, value)` | `header(name, value)` |
| `c.set()` and `c.get()`, `c.var` | `state` from `createApp({ middleware })`, and `user` from auth |
| `HTTPException` | `httpError(status, message)`, `notFound()`, `forbidden()`, `badRequest()` ([errors](routes.md#errors)) |
| `hono/bearer-auth`, `hono/jwt`, `hono/basic-auth` | `createApp({ auth })` with `bearer(...)` or `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }`, and the route's `auth` option ([auth](auth.md)) |
| `hono/cors` | `createApp({ cors: { origin: [...] } })` |
| `hono/secure-headers` | Built in: security headers on every response ([security](security.md)) |
| `hono/logger`, `hono/request-id` | `createApp({ logging: { requests: true } })` and `X-Request-Id` ([observability](observability.md)) |
| `hono/timeout` | `createApp({ requestTimeoutMs })` and the route's `timeoutMs` ([security](security.md#request-timeouts)) |
| `hono.route("/books", books)` sub-apps | Route files, grouped into [modules](modules.md) for larger features |
| `basePath("/v1")` | `apiVersion("v1", routes)`, with an OpenAPI document per version ([API versions](routes.md#api-versions)) |
| `@hono/zod-openapi`, `@hono/swagger-ui` | Generated: `GET /openapi.json` from the route schemas |
| Hono RPC (`hc<AppType>`) | The OpenAPI document for client generators; MCP tools for AI agents |
| `hono/streaming` (`streamSSE`) | `return ctx.ai.stream(...).toResponse()` for model output, or a `Response` with a `ReadableStream` |
| `c.env` bindings and `process.env` | `config({ schema })` in `src/config.ts` ([configuration](config.md)) |
| `app.request()` in tests | `app.request(path, { method, json, as: user })` with a signed-in test user ([testing](testing.md)) |
| `export default hono` | `export default app` (Bun, Deno, Workers) or `app.listen()` on Node.js ([deployment](deploy.md)) |

## 4. Share auth between both

During the migration, Hono and Inferlo routes must accept the same credentials. Put the check in one function and use it from both:

```ts
// src/auth-check.ts
export async function userFromToken(token: string | undefined) {
  if (!token) return null;
  const session = await sessions.findByToken(token); // your existing lookup
  return session ? { id: session.userId, roles: session.roles } : null;
}
```

```ts
// Hono middleware, as before
export const requireUser = createMiddleware(async (c, next) => {
  const user = await userFromToken(c.req.header("authorization")?.replace(/^Bearer /, ""));
  if (!user) return c.json({ error: "Sign in required" }, 401);
  c.set("user", user);
  await next();
});
```

```ts
// src/inferlo/auth.ts
import { bearer } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { userFromToken } from "../auth-check.ts";

export const auth = bearer((token) => userFromToken(token));
```

A user needs an `id`, and `roles` for role-based routes. For cookies or other schemes, write `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }`; `req` is the same standard `Request` Hono gives you as `c.req.raw`.

## 5. Keep your data layer, then adopt models where they fit

Inferlo handlers can call any database code you already have (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely, a D1 or Postgres client): import it and use it in the handler. You do not have to move data access to switch routes.

For new tables, use Inferlo [models](database.md): validated inserts and updates, typed queries, relations, pagination and generated migrations (`inferlo db migrate`). Inferlo models expect a `uuid` `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` columns and snake_case column names, so existing tables that differ are best left with your current code.

## 6. Move the tests

```ts
// Before: Hono's app.request with a token
const res = await hono.request("/tickets", { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ title: "Printer" }) });

// After: signed in as a test user, JSON body without headers
import { readJson } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/testing";

const res = await app.request("/tickets", { method: "POST", json: { title: "Printer" }, as: { id: "u1", roles: [] } });
const ticket = await readJson(res, 201);
```

Tests through the Hono app (`hono.request(...)`) keep working during the migration, because the catch-all passes requests on to Inferlo.

## 7. Remove Hono

When the last Hono route is gone, export the Inferlo app instead:

```ts
// src/index.ts on Bun, Deno or Cloudflare Workers
import { app } from "./inferlo/app.ts";
export default app;
```

```ts
// src/server.ts on Node.js
import { app } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const server = await app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log(`Listening on http://localhost:${server.port}`);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => void app.close({ delayMs: 5000 }));
```

Then remove `hono`, its validator and OpenAPI packages and the middleware Inferlo replaced. Compare your app with a new project from `npx @browserlessapi/inferlo new` for the recommended layout, configuration and AGENTS.md for AI coding tools.

## Checklist

- [ ] `hono.all("*", (c) => inferlo.fetch(c.req.raw))` after every Hono route
- [ ] One auth check shared by Hono and Inferlo
- [ ] Each moved route: schemas for its input, the right `auth`, `status(201)` where clients expect it, the Hono route deleted, a test with `app.request`
- [ ] Hono's CORS and security header middleware scoped to Hono routes (Inferlo sends its own)
- [ ] Clients told about the new error format, if they read error bodies
- [ ] Hono removed, `export default app` (or `app.listen()` and `app.close()` on Node.js)

If you only want Inferlo's AI features inside Hono and no migration, use `c.var.ai` from [`@browserlessapi/inferlo/hono`](integrations.md#hono) instead.

---

# Migrate from Koa

This guide moves an existing Koa app (Koa 2 or 3) to Inferlo one route at a time. The app keeps running in the same Node.js process and keeps its URLs during the whole migration: Inferlo answers the routes you have moved, Koa answers the rest. Nothing has to be rewritten in one go.

What you gain on every route you move: validation and types from one schema instead of hand-written checks, routes private by default, the same error format everywhere (`ILxxxx` codes), a database layer with migrations, rate limits, background jobs, an OpenAPI document and an MCP server generated from the routes, and AI models through `ctx.ai`. See [comparison](comparison.md) for the bigger picture.

## 1. Add Inferlo next to Koa

```bash
npm install @browserlessapi/inferlo
```

Create an empty Inferlo app beside your Koa code, for example in `src/inferlo/app.ts`:

```ts
// src/inferlo/app.ts
import { createApp } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { auth } from "./auth.ts";
import * as tickets from "./routes/tickets.ts";

export const app = createApp({
  name: "helpdesk",
  routes: [tickets],
  auth,
  logging: { requests: true },
});
```

Mount it with `toKoaMiddleware(app, { fallthrough: true })` from `@browserlessapi/inferlo/koa`, **before** your Koa router:

```ts
// src/server.ts (your existing Koa entry point)
import Koa from "koa";
import Router from "@koa/router";
import bodyParser from "@koa/bodyparser";
import { toKoaMiddleware } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/koa";
import { app as inferlo } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const koa = new Koa();
const router = new Router();

router.get("/users/:id", requireUser, getUser);   // not moved yet: Koa answers

koa.use(bodyParser());
koa.use(toKoaMiddleware(inferlo, { fallthrough: true })); // Inferlo's routes, OpenAPI and MCP; everything else goes on
koa.use(router.routes()).use(router.allowedMethods());

koa.listen(3000);
```

With `fallthrough: true`, Inferlo answers only the requests it has a route for (method and path) and its own endpoints (`/openapi.json`, `/mcp`, health, metrics and CORS preflights of its paths), and calls `next()` for everything else, so Koa's router keeps answering what it had, including other methods on the same path. As you move routes, more requests stop at Inferlo; nothing else changes.

- Body parsers: when `@koa/bodyparser` or `koa-bodyparser` runs first, Inferlo uses `ctx.request.body`; when Inferlo comes first, it reads the request itself. Either order works.
- Middleware added before Inferlo (logging, request ids) also runs for its requests. Inferlo answers moved routes itself, so Koa middleware after it (and code that runs after `await next()` and sets `ctx.body`) does not touch Inferlo's responses.
- To keep the new routes under their own path for a while, use a prefix instead: `koa.use(toKoaMiddleware(inferlo, { prefix: "/v2" }))` serves the app under `/v2` and passes other paths on. To use only Inferlo's AI features in Koa middleware, see [`inferloAI()`](integrations.md#koa).

## 2. Move one route

Before, in Koa with `@koa/router` and a hand-written check:

```ts
router.post("/tickets", requireUser, async (ctx) => {
  const { title, priority = "normal" } = ctx.request.body ?? {};
  if (typeof title !== "string" || title.length < 3 || title.length > 200) ctx.throw(422, "title must be 3 to 200 characters");
  if (!["low", "normal", "urgent"].includes(priority)) ctx.throw(422, "invalid priority");
  const ticket = await tickets.insert({ title, priority, ownerId: ctx.state.user.id });
  ctx.status = 201;
  ctx.body = ticket;
});
```

After, in Inferlo:

```ts
// src/inferlo/routes/tickets.ts
import { route, t } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { tickets } from "../../db.ts"; // your existing data access code

export const createTicket = route
  .post("/tickets", {
    body: t.object({
      title: t.string().min(3).max(200),
      priority: t.enum(["low", "normal", "urgent"]).default("normal"),
    }),
    summary: "Create a ticket",
  })
  .handle(async ({ body, user, status }) => {
    status(201);
    return tickets.insert({ ...body, ownerId: user.id });
  });
```

Then delete the Koa route. Requests to `POST /tickets` now stop at Inferlo, at the same URL.

- The schema replaces the hand-written checks (or `koa-joi-router`, `koa-zod-router` and similar): invalid input gets `422` with IL1001 and every problem listed, and `body` is typed. `query` and `params` schemas convert and check `ctx.query` and `ctx.params`.
- The route is private by default: `user` is the signed-in user (no more `ctx.state.user`), and requests without one get `401` (IL3001). This replaces `requireUser`, `koa-jwt` or `koa-passport` checks. Add `auth: "public"` to routes anyone may call, or a role name such as `auth: "admin"`.
- Return the value instead of setting `ctx.body`; call `status(201)` instead of `ctx.status = 201`. `undefined` sends `204`. Return a `Response` for anything that is not JSON.
- Throw `notFound()`, `forbidden()` or `httpError(409, "...")` instead of `ctx.throw(...)` or `http-errors`.
- The error format changes to Inferlo's `{ "error": { "code", "message", ... } }`. If clients parse error bodies, tell them, or move routes in groups that one client uses.

## 3. Map Koa concepts to Inferlo

| Koa | Inferlo |
|---|---|
| `router.get(path, ...middleware, handler)` (`@koa/router`) | `export const x = route.get(path, options).handle(handler)` in a routes file, registered with `createApp({ routes: [file] })` |
| `ctx.params`, `ctx.query`, `ctx.request.body` | `params`, `query`, `body` in the handler context, validated by schemas ([schemas](schema.md)) |
| `ctx.body = value`, `ctx.status = 201` | `return value` and `status(201)` |
| `ctx.set(name, value)` | `header(name, value)` |
| `ctx.state` | `state` from `createApp({ middleware })`, and `user` from auth |
| `ctx.throw(404)`, `http-errors` | `notFound()`, `forbidden()`, `badRequest()`, `httpError(status, message)` ([errors](routes.md#errors)) |
| Error-handling middleware (`try { await next() } catch`) | Built in: every error becomes the standard error body, and unexpected errors are logged with secrets redacted |
| `koa-compose`, middleware chains per route | `createApp({ middleware })` for cross-cutting code, the route's `auth`, `permission` and `rateLimit` options for checks |
| `koa-jwt`, `koa-passport`, custom auth middleware | `createApp({ auth })` with `bearer(...)` or `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }`, and the route's `auth` option ([auth](auth.md)) |
| `koa-bodyparser`, `@koa/bodyparser`, `@koa/multer` | Built in for JSON and forms, with `createApp({ maxBodySize })` |
| `@koa/cors` | `createApp({ cors: { origin: [...] } })` |
| `koa-helmet` | Built in: security headers on every response ([security](security.md)) |
| `koa-ratelimit` | The route's `rateLimit: { max, per, by }`, with memory or Postgres stores ([routes](routes.md)) |
| `koa-logger`, request id middleware | `createApp({ logging: { requests: true } })` and `X-Request-Id` ([observability](observability.md)) |
| `koa-mount`, nested routers with a prefix | Route files, grouped into [modules](modules.md); `apiVersion("v1", routes)` for `/v1` ([API versions](routes.md#api-versions)) |
| `koa-swagger-decorator`, `koa2-swagger-ui` | Generated: `GET /openapi.json` from the route schemas |
| `ctx.req` streaming, server-sent events | `return ctx.ai.stream(...).toResponse()` for model output, or a `Response` with a `ReadableStream` |
| `dotenv`, `process.env` | `config({ schema })` in `src/config.ts` ([configuration](config.md)) |
| `supertest(koa.callback())` in tests | `app.request(path, { method, json, as: user })` with a signed-in test user ([testing](testing.md)) |
| `koa.listen(3000)` | `app.listen(3000)` and `app.close()` on SIGTERM ([deployment](deploy.md)) |

`koa-static`, `koa-views` and `koa-session` have no Inferlo equivalent yet: keep them in Koa (they are not routes you need to move), or serve static files from a CDN or reverse proxy.

## 4. Share auth between both

During the migration, Koa and Inferlo routes must accept the same credentials. Put the check in one function and use it from both:

```ts
// src/auth-check.ts
export async function userFromToken(token: string | undefined) {
  if (!token) return null;
  const session = await sessions.findByToken(token); // your existing lookup
  return session ? { id: session.userId, roles: session.roles } : null;
}
```

```ts
// Koa middleware, as before
export const requireUser: Koa.Middleware = async (ctx, next) => {
  const user = await userFromToken(ctx.get("authorization").replace(/^Bearer /, "") || undefined);
  if (!user) ctx.throw(401, "Sign in required");
  ctx.state.user = user;
  await next();
};
```

```ts
// src/inferlo/auth.ts
import { bearer } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { userFromToken } from "../auth-check.ts";

export const auth = bearer((token) => userFromToken(token));
```

A user needs an `id`, and `roles` for role-based routes. For cookie sessions or other schemes, write `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }`; `req` is a standard `Request` with the same headers and cookies Koa sees.

## 5. Keep your data layer, then adopt models where they fit

Inferlo handlers can call any database code you already have (Knex, Sequelize, TypeORM, Prisma, Drizzle, a `pg` pool): import it and use it in the handler. You do not have to move data access to switch routes.

For new tables, use Inferlo [models](database.md): validated inserts and updates, typed queries, relations, pagination and generated migrations (`inferlo db migrate`). Inferlo models expect a `uuid` `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` columns and snake_case column names, so existing tables that differ are best left with your current code.

## 6. Move the tests

```ts
// Before: supertest with a token
const res = await request(koa.callback()).post("/tickets").set("authorization", `Bearer ${token}`).send({ title: "Printer" });

// After: signed in as a test user, without a server
import { readJson } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/testing";

const res = await app.request("/tickets", { method: "POST", json: { title: "Printer" }, as: { id: "u1", roles: [] } });
const ticket = await readJson(res, 201);
```

Supertest tests against `koa.callback()` keep working during the migration, because moved routes are answered at the same URLs.

## 7. Remove Koa

When the last Koa route is gone, start the Inferlo app directly:

```ts
// src/server.ts
import { app } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const server = await app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log(`Listening on http://localhost:${server.port}`);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => void app.close({ delayMs: 5000 }));
```

Then remove `koa`, `@koa/router`, the body parser and the middleware Inferlo replaced. Compare your app with a new project from `npx @browserlessapi/inferlo new` for the recommended layout, configuration and AGENTS.md for AI coding tools.

## Checklist

- [ ] `koa.use(toKoaMiddleware(inferlo, { fallthrough: true }))` before the Koa router
- [ ] One auth check shared by Koa and Inferlo
- [ ] Each moved route: schemas for its input, the right `auth`, `status(201)` where clients expect it, the Koa route deleted, a test with `app.request`
- [ ] Koa's CORS and helmet middleware scoped to Koa routes (Inferlo sends its own headers)
- [ ] Clients told about the new error format, if they read error bodies
- [ ] Koa removed, `app.listen()` and `app.close()` on SIGTERM

If you only want Inferlo's AI features inside Koa and no migration, use `ctx.ai` from [`@browserlessapi/inferlo/koa`](integrations.md#koa) instead.

---

# Migrate from Fastify

This guide moves an existing Fastify app (Fastify 5) to Inferlo one route at a time. The app keeps running in the same Node.js process and keeps its URLs during the whole migration: Inferlo answers the routes you have moved, Fastify answers the rest. Nothing has to be rewritten in one go.

What you gain on every route you move: validation and types from one schema instead of JSON schemas plus separate TypeScript types, routes private by default, the same error format everywhere (`ILxxxx` codes), a database layer with migrations, rate limits, background jobs, an OpenAPI document and an MCP server generated from the routes, and AI models through `ctx.ai`. See [comparison](comparison.md) for the bigger picture.

## 1. Add Inferlo next to Fastify

```bash
npm install @browserlessapi/inferlo
```

Create an empty Inferlo app beside your Fastify code, for example in `src/inferlo/app.ts`:

```ts
// src/inferlo/app.ts
import { createApp } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { auth } from "./auth.ts";
import * as tickets from "./routes/tickets.ts";

export const app = createApp({
  name: "helpdesk",
  routes: [tickets],
  auth,
  logging: { requests: true },
});
```

Register it with `inferloPlugin` from `@browserlessapi/inferlo/fastify` and `fallthrough: true`:

```ts
// src/server.ts (your existing Fastify entry point)
import Fastify from "fastify";
import { inferloPlugin } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/fastify";
import { app as inferlo } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const fastify = Fastify({ logger: true });

await fastify.register(cors, { origin: ["https://app.example.com"] });
fastify.get("/users/:id", { preHandler: requireUser }, getUser);   // not moved yet: Fastify answers

await fastify.register(inferloPlugin, { app: inferlo, fallthrough: true }); // Inferlo's routes, OpenAPI and MCP

await fastify.listen({ port: 3000 });
```

With `fallthrough: true`, Inferlo answers only the requests it has a route for (method and path) and its own endpoints (`/openapi.json`, `/mcp`, health, metrics and CORS preflights of its paths), in an `onRequest` hook, before Fastify reads the body. Every other request goes on to Fastify's router as before, including other methods on the same path and Fastify's own 404 handler. As you move routes, more requests stop at Inferlo; nothing else changes.

- Order: where you register the plugin does not change which requests Inferlo answers. `onRequest` hooks added before it on the root instance (request ids, logging) also run for Inferlo's requests; hooks added after it, hooks inside encapsulated plugins and the later hooks (`preParsing`, `preValidation`, `preHandler`, `onSend`) do not, because Inferlo answers the request itself.
- Body parsing: Inferlo reads the request body itself (JSON, forms, its own `maxBodySize`), so Fastify's content type parsers and `bodyLimit` stay as they are for your Fastify routes.
- Global plugins that change responses (`@fastify/cors`, `@fastify/helmet`, `@fastify/compress`) work through `onSend` and similar hooks, so they do not apply to Inferlo's responses. Inferlo sends its own CORS and security headers; configure them in `createApp`.
- To keep the new routes under their own path for a while, add a prefix: `{ app: inferlo, prefix: "/v2", fallthrough: true }` answers the app's routes under `/v2` only. Without `fallthrough`, `{ app, prefix: "/v2" }` gives the whole prefix to Inferlo, including its 404s. To use only Inferlo's AI features in Fastify routes, see [`fastify.ai` and `request.ai`](integrations.md#fastify-1).

## 2. Move one route

Before, in Fastify with a JSON schema, a TypeScript type for the same body and an auth hook:

```ts
interface CreateTicket { title: string; priority?: "low" | "normal" | "urgent" }

fastify.post<{ Body: CreateTicket }>(
  "/tickets",
  {
    preHandler: requireUser,
    schema: {
      body: {
        type: "object",
        required: ["title"],
        properties: {
          title: { type: "string", minLength: 3, maxLength: 200 },
          priority: { type: "string", enum: ["low", "normal", "urgent"], default: "normal" },
        },
      },
    },
  },
  async (request, reply) => {
    const ticket = await tickets.insert({ ...request.body, ownerId: request.user.id });
    return reply.code(201).send(ticket);
  },
);
```

After, in Inferlo:

```ts
// src/inferlo/routes/tickets.ts
import { route, t } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { tickets } from "../../db.ts"; // your existing data access code

export const createTicket = route
  .post("/tickets", {
    body: t.object({
      title: t.string().min(3).max(200),
      priority: t.enum(["low", "normal", "urgent"]).default("normal"),
    }),
    summary: "Create a ticket",
  })
  .handle(async ({ body, user, status }) => {
    status(201);
    return tickets.insert({ ...body, ownerId: user.id });
  });
```

Then delete the Fastify route. Requests to `POST /tickets` now stop at Inferlo, at the same URL.

- One `t.*` schema replaces the JSON schema and the TypeScript type (or a TypeBox or Zod type provider): invalid input gets `422` with IL1001 and every problem listed, and `body` is typed. `query` and `params` schemas replace `schema.querystring` and `schema.params` and convert strings to numbers and booleans the same way. `response` replaces `schema.response` for the OpenAPI document.
- The route is private by default: `user` is the signed-in user (no more `request.user` from a decorator), and requests without one get `401` (IL3001). This replaces `preHandler: requireUser`, `@fastify/jwt` with `request.jwtVerify()` and `@fastify/auth`. Add `auth: "public"` to routes anyone may call, or a role name such as `auth: "admin"`.
- Return the value; call `status(201)` instead of `reply.code(201)` and `header(name, value)` instead of `reply.header(...)`. `undefined` sends `204`. Return a `Response` for anything that is not JSON.
- Throw `notFound()`, `forbidden()` or `httpError(409, "...")` instead of `reply.code(404).send(...)` or `@fastify/sensible`'s `reply.notFound()` and `fastify.httpErrors`.
- The error format changes from Fastify's `{ statusCode, error, message }` to Inferlo's `{ "error": { "code", "message", ... } }`. If clients parse error bodies, tell them, or move routes in groups that one client uses.

## 3. Map Fastify concepts to Inferlo

| Fastify | Inferlo |
|---|---|
| `fastify.get(path, options, handler)`, route shorthand and `fastify.route({ ... })` | `export const x = route.get(path, options).handle(handler)` in a routes file, registered with `createApp({ routes: [file] })` |
| `schema: { body, querystring, params }` (Ajv JSON schemas), type providers | `body`, `query` and `params` with `t.*` schemas: validation and types from one definition ([schemas](schema.md)) |
| `schema.response` and fast-json-stringify | `response: schema` on the route, used for OpenAPI |
| `request.body`, `request.query`, `request.params` | `body`, `query`, `params` in the handler context |
| `return value`, `reply.code(201)`, `reply.header()` | `return value`, `status(201)`, `header(name, value)` |
| Plugins with `fastify.register(plugin, { prefix })` and encapsulation | Route files grouped into [modules](modules.md) with explicit `imports`; `apiVersion("v1", routes)` for `/v1` ([API versions](routes.md#api-versions)) |
| `fastify-plugin` to share decorators | Not needed: modules export plain functions in `provides`, called directly |
| `fastify.decorate("db", ...)`, `decorateRequest` | Import the value, or use `ctx.db`, `ctx.ai`, `ctx.jobs` and `state` from middleware |
| Hooks: `onRequest`, `preHandler` for auth and checks | The route's `auth`, `permission` and `rateLimit` options; `createApp({ middleware })` for cross-cutting code |
| Hooks: `onSend`, `onResponse`, `onError` | `createApp({ middleware })` (it sees the response), request logs with timing, and logged errors |
| `fastify.setErrorHandler`, `setNotFoundHandler` | Built in: every error becomes the standard error body; unexpected errors are logged with secrets redacted |
| `@fastify/jwt`, `@fastify/auth`, `@fastify/basic-auth` | `createApp({ auth })` with `bearer(...)` or `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }` ([auth](auth.md)) |
| `@fastify/cors` | `createApp({ cors: { origin: [...] } })` |
| `@fastify/helmet` | Built in: security headers on every response ([security](security.md)) |
| `@fastify/rate-limit` | The route's `rateLimit: { max, per, by }`, with memory or Postgres stores ([routes](routes.md)) |
| `@fastify/formbody`, `bodyLimit` | Built in for JSON and forms, with `createApp({ maxBodySize })` |
| `@fastify/env`, `env-schema` | `config({ schema })` in `src/config.ts` ([configuration](config.md)) |
| `@fastify/swagger`, `@fastify/swagger-ui` | Generated: `GET /openapi.json` from the route schemas |
| `@fastify/under-pressure`, health check plugins | `createApp({ health: true })` with `/health` and `/ready` ([observability](observability.md)) |
| `fastify-metrics` | `createApp({ metrics })` with `/metrics` in the Prometheus format |
| Pino logger, `request.log`, `genReqId` | `createApp({ logging: { format: "json", requests: true } })` and `X-Request-Id` ([observability](observability.md)) |
| `@fastify/schedule`, queue plugins | `job(...)`, `cron(...)` and `inferlo worker` ([jobs](jobs.md)) |
| `reply.sse(...)`, streaming replies | `return ctx.ai.stream(...).toResponse()` for model output, or a `Response` with a `ReadableStream` |
| `fastify.inject()` in tests | `app.request(path, { method, json, as: user })` with a signed-in test user ([testing](testing.md)) |
| `fastify.listen()` and `fastify.close()` | `app.listen(3000)` and `app.close()` on SIGTERM ([deployment](deploy.md)) |

`@fastify/static`, `@fastify/view`, `@fastify/multipart`, `@fastify/websocket` and `@fastify/session` have no Inferlo equivalent yet: keep those routes in Fastify (they keep working next to Inferlo), or serve static files from a CDN or reverse proxy.

## 4. Share auth between both

During the migration, Fastify and Inferlo routes must accept the same credentials. Put the check in one function and use it from both:

```ts
// src/auth-check.ts
export async function userFromToken(token: string | undefined) {
  if (!token) return null;
  const session = await sessions.findByToken(token); // your existing lookup
  return session ? { id: session.userId, roles: session.roles } : null;
}
```

```ts
// Fastify preHandler hook, as before
export async function requireUser(request: FastifyRequest, reply: FastifyReply) {
  const user = await userFromToken(request.headers.authorization?.replace(/^Bearer /, ""));
  if (!user) return reply.code(401).send({ message: "Sign in required" });
  request.user = user;
}
```

```ts
// src/inferlo/auth.ts
import { bearer } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo";
import { userFromToken } from "../auth-check.ts";

export const auth = bearer((token) => userFromToken(token));
```

A user needs an `id`, and `roles` for role-based routes. For cookie sessions or other schemes, write `auth: { resolve(req) { ... } }`; `req` is a standard `Request` with the same headers and cookies Fastify sees.

## 5. Keep your data layer, then adopt models where they fit

Inferlo handlers can call any database code you already have (`@fastify/postgres`'s pool, Knex, Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM, MikroORM): import it and use it in the handler. Values that only exist as Fastify decorators (`fastify.pg`) need to be created in a module both sides import, for example a shared `pg` pool. You do not have to move data access to switch routes.

For new tables, use Inferlo [models](database.md): validated inserts and updates, typed queries, relations, pagination and generated migrations (`inferlo db migrate`). Inferlo models expect a `uuid` `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` columns and snake_case column names, so existing tables that differ are best left with your current code.

## 6. Move the tests

```ts
// Before: fastify.inject with a token
const res = await fastify.inject({ method: "POST", url: "/tickets", headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, payload: { title: "Printer" } });

// After: signed in as a test user, without a server
import { readJson } from "@browserlessapi/inferlo/testing";

const res = await app.request("/tickets", { method: "POST", json: { title: "Printer" }, as: { id: "u1", roles: [] } });
const ticket = await readJson(res, 201);
```

`fastify.inject()` tests keep working during the migration, because moved routes are answered at the same URLs.

## 7. Remove Fastify

When the last Fastify route is gone, start the Inferlo app directly:

```ts
// src/server.ts
import { app } from "./inferlo/app.ts";

const server = await app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log(`Listening on http://localhost:${server.port}`);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => void app.close({ delayMs: 5000 }));
```

Then remove `fastify` and the plugins Inferlo replaced. Compare your app with a new project from `npx @browserlessapi/inferlo new` for the recommended layout, configuration and AGENTS.md for AI coding tools.

## Checklist

- [ ] `fastify.register(inferloPlugin, { app: inferlo, fallthrough: true })`
- [ ] One auth check shared by Fastify and Inferlo
- [ ] Each moved route: schemas for its input, the right `auth`, `status(201)` where clients expect it, the Fastify route deleted, a test with `app.request`
- [ ] CORS and security headers configured in `createApp` for Inferlo's routes (Fastify's `onSend` plugins do not touch them)
- [ ] Clients told about the new error format, if they read error bodies
- [ ] Fastify removed, `app.listen()` and `app.close()` on SIGTERM

If you only want Inferlo's AI features inside Fastify and no migration, use `fastify.ai` and `request.ai` from [`@browserlessapi/inferlo/fastify`](integrations.md#fastify-1) instead.
